title: Malva pudding
skill: A sponge pudding soaked in a warm butter-cream sauce

move.title: A sponge that drinks its sauce
move.body: Malva pudding is South Africa's favorite dessert: a soft, caramel-colored sponge made with apricot jam, soaked while it's hot in a warm sauce of cream, butter, and sugar. Today you'll beat eggs and sugar until thick, bake the sponge, and pour the sauce over so it soaks all the way through.

why.title: Beat until thick
why.body: Beating eggs and sugar for several minutes traps air, and the mix turns pale and thick. That air helps the sponge rise light enough to soak up the sauce.

why.title: Vinegar and baking soda
why.body: Vinegar is an acid. With the baking soda, it makes bubbles that lift the batter. You can't taste it after baking.

why.title: Hot sponge, hot sauce
why.body: A hot sponge is full of open bubbles, like a sponge for dishes. Hot sauce poured over right away soaks all the way through. A cold sponge just lets it pool on top.

wrong.fix: The pudding cooled before the sauce went on, or wasn't poked. Poke more holes and let it sit longer.
Bake 5 more minutes and test again.
The eggs and sugar weren't beaten long enough. Beat until thick and pale next time.
Lay foil over it for the last 10 minutes.

quiz.q: Why beat the eggs and sugar so long?
choices: To trap air so the sponge is light

quiz.q: When does the sauce go on?
choices: As soon as the pudding comes out, while it's hot
quiz.explain: A hot sponge soaks it up.

choices: Reacts with baking soda to make bubbles
quiz.explain: You can't taste it after baking.

ingredients.text: a little more, soft, for the dish

steps.text: Put a rack in the middle of the oven and heat it to 350°F. Brush the baking dish with soft butter.
Melt the pudding's 2 tablespoons of butter in the small bowl in the microwave. Stir in the milk and vinegar.
Beat the eggs and the pudding's sugar in the large bowl with the whisk until pale and thick. Whisk in the jam.
steps.look: Pale, thick, and falling from the whisk in a ribbon.

steps.text: Wash your hands with soap, and throw away the eggshells.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, and salt in the medium bowl.
Fold the flour mix and the milk mix into the eggs in turns, a third at a time, just until smooth.
steps.tip: Don't taste the raw batter. It has raw egg.

steps.text: Scrape the batter into the dish and bake until deep golden brown.
steps.look: Deep caramel brown, and springy when touched.

steps.text: While it bakes, heat the cream, the sauce's butter and sugar, and the hot water in the saucepan over medium heat, stirring, until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves. Stir in the vanilla.
With oven mitts, pull out the rack. Push a toothpick into the center. If it comes out clean, it's done. If not, bake 5 more minutes.

target.look: A clean toothpick from the center

steps.text: Set the dish on the rack and turn off the oven. Poke holes all over the hot pudding with the fork.
Pour the warm sauce slowly over the whole pudding. Let it soak in before serving warm.
steps.look: The sauce has soaked in, with a glossy top.

sauce.text: Time the sauce for the last 5 minutes of baking: heat the cream, sauce butter, sugar, and hot water until smooth, then add the vanilla.

check.text: Check the sponge's center: 200°F. Under, bake 3 minutes more.

poke.text: Turn off the oven. Poke the hot pudding all over with the fork.

soak.text: Pour the sauce over slowly and let it soak in. Serve warm, with the custard.

add.text: Separate 3 eggs, putting the yolks in the heatproof bowl. Save the whites for another dish.
add.tip: Pass the yolk between the shell halves over a small bowl.

add.text: Wash your hands, and throw away the shells.
Whisk the custard's sugar into the yolks. Heat the custard's milk in the light saucepan until steaming, then whisk it slowly into the yolks.
Pour it back into the saucepan and stir over low heat until it coats the spoon. Stir in the vanilla.

move.title: Sponge, sauce, and a stirred custard
move.body: In South Africa, malva pudding comes to the table hot, soaked in its butter-cream sauce, with a pour of warm custard. You'll bake the sponge to 200°F, time the sauce to meet it the minute it comes out, and stir a custard on the stove to 175°F, thick enough to coat a spoon.

wrong.fix: The pudding cooled before the sauce went on, or wasn't poked. Poke more holes and let it sit longer.
Bake 5 more minutes and test again.
The eggs and sugar weren't beaten long enough. Beat until thick and pale next time.
Lay foil over it for the last 10 minutes.
It got too hot. Pour it through a strainer, and take it off the heat sooner next time.

quiz.q: What temperature is a stirred custard done at?
choices: About 175°F, thick enough to coat a spoon

quiz.q: When does the sauce go on the pudding?
choices: The minute it comes out, while both are hot
quiz.explain: A hot sponge soaks it up.

quiz.q: What temperature is the sponge done at in the center?

add.title: A stirred custard
add.body: Egg yolks thicken milk as they heat. Stirred over low heat, they thicken smoothly between 170 and 180°F. Above about 185°F, they scramble.

add.title: 200°F in the sponge
add.body: The sponge is set at about 200°F in the center, before the top over-browns.
